title: Thirty-eight metrics in a dozen passes
subtitle: A hand-written CUDA engine for Blackwell that scores thousands of embedding clusters at once and searches them with the same kernels

stats.label: faster centroid family at 100,000 members after the rewrite
minimum recall at ten against exact search, held in CI
lines of Rust around about 11,000 of CUDA

lede: My distillation research produces millions of embeddings grouped into clusters, and it needs to know, for every cluster, how tight it is, whether it has sub-structure, how it relates to its neighbours, and how much information it carries. That is thirty-eight statistics per cluster, over vectors of 1,024 dimensions, for thousands of clusters at a time. I wrote a CUDA engine for it, from Rust against the driver API, compiled natively for Blackwell, with a CPU reference and equivalence tests for every kernel. The same engine does exact, inverted-file and lattice vector search, and a fused variant computes cluster health as a side effect of the search it was already doing.
quote: The quadratic distance matrix never exists.
evidence: CUDA kernel development: a hand-written CUDA engine for NVIDIA Blackwell scoring thirty-eight statistics per cluster over 1,024-dimension vectors, with no sampling and no caps.
Embedding analytics and cluster metrics: the centroid family made 11x faster at 100,000 members, and two-means at about 500K/s members with no atomics.
Vector search and ANN indexes: exact, inverted-file and lattice search on the same kernels, with recall at ten held at 0.85 or better against exact search in CI.
Rust systems engineering: 11,600 lines of Rust around about 11,000 of CUDA, reaching the CUDA 13 driver API through a 300-line safe wrapper.
author: Corey James
